drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A manufacturing customer's C T O forwards you a rival lab's launch post.
drills.answer_line: SAM: That's the core of it. The answer is C.
drills.stem: A rival lab's launch post says its new model beats Claude on a coding benchmark, from runs the lab did itself. The CTO asks whether to switch the team's coding agent. What do you do first?

options.A: Ask the lab for its harness and settings, and accept the result once disclosed
options.B: Point to an independent leaderboard where Claude ranks higher
options.C: Run both models on a small private eval built from the team's own repositories and tickets, comparing cost per task as well as score
options.D: Tell the CTO vendor-reported numbers are marketing and can be ignored

drills.why: A decision about the team's work needs a test on their work, with cost per task. A still trusts the vendor's frame, B answers a general question a public board cannot see their code for, D dismisses evidence the CTO will keep hearing.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each item, name the layer.
drills.prompt: Name the layer. 1) An admin setting that turns a model off for EU staff. 2) Buying Claude in Microsoft Foundry to draw down an Azure commitment. 3) An open-source framework for multi-agent workflows. 4) Web search built into the API.
drills.answer: 1) Enterprise wrapper. 2) Route to market. 3) Agent stack. 4) Developer platform.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.prompt: True or false? 1) Arena's text leaderboard measures which model completes tasks best. 2) SWE-bench Verified is still the best public test of coding agents. 3) On an agent benchmark, one model can score differently under different harnesses. 4) A score a vendor publishes for its own model is independent evidence.
drills.answer: 1) False: human preference, not task success. 2) False: OpenAI stopped reporting it, citing contamination and flawed tests. 3) True. 4) False: vendor-reported.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A bank's board member
drills.answer_line: SAM: Yes. A is disclosure, B is scope.
drills.scenario: Board member quotes a market report
drills.stem: Choose two. A bank's board member quotes a market report showing Anthropic far ahead of Google in enterprise AI. Which two caveats should you raise?

options.A: The publisher is an Anthropic investor
options.B: It counts API spend, not spend bundled into productivity suites
options.C: Survey-based reports are made up and should never be cited
options.D: The lead proves Claude is the right model for the bank's use case
options.E: The report is unreliable because it is recent

drills.why: A is disclosure, B is scope. C overcorrects: a survey with a stated method is evidence with limits. D confuses market share with fit. E is backwards.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A logistics company runs on A W S
drills.stem: The company has a large AWS commitment and procurement will not sign with a new vendor this year. The team wants Claude for document agents and wants to trial an OpenAI model against it. What do you recommend?

options.A: Sign a direct contract with Anthropic and another with OpenAI
options.B: Buy both through Amazon Bedrock on the existing commitment
options.D: Wait for next year's procurement cycle

drills.why: Bedrock carries both Claude and OpenAI models on the existing commitment, no new vendor. A needs the contracts procurement ruled out, C swaps in a model nobody asked for, D loses a year. Bedrock lacks some Claude features such as Managed Agents (episode four).

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four skills from this episode
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Six layers: better at which layer?
drills.prompt: Name the four skills from this episode, and the question each one makes you ask.
drills.answer: Six layers: better at which layer? Benchmarks: who ran it, and what does it measure? Market reports: who published it, and what does it count? Slow and fast facts: true next month?

In this episode: Place any vendor on six layers
Read a benchmark: who ran it, what it measures
Read a market report and name its source
Slow facts to quote, fast facts to check
The route through episodes one to eight
Cold open: the launch post: A rival lab claims a coding win from its own runs
The CTO asks whether to switch the team's coding agent
Four responses: ask, point, test, dismiss
The six layers: Model, developer platform, agent stack, coding agent, enterprise wrapper, route to market
Model: DeepSeek open weights; provenance travels with the model
Developer platform: OpenAI Responses API built-in tools
Agent stack: Google ADK, Apache 2.0, five languages, model-agnostic
Coding agent: Cursor builds own models; SpaceX now owns it
Wrapper: Claude inside Microsoft 365 Copilot; route: Bedrock sells OpenAI too
Reading a benchmark: Four questions: who ran it, what it measures, contaminated, saturated
Vendor-reported: own harness, own settings, chosen frame
Artificial Analysis: independent composite with cost per task
Arena: human preference; Terminal-Bench: harness matters
SWE-bench Verified and Pro lost OpenAI's backing in 2026
Reading a market report: Menlo is an Anthropic investor, and says so
Survey of about 400 US decision-makers: estimates, not audited revenue
API spend only: Google's figure excludes Workspace and Gemini app bundles
Read the method before the headline
Slow facts and fast facts: Slow: architecture, licences, protocols, governance, business models, channels
Fast: prices, ranks, context windows, versions, cloud line-ups
MCP, AGENTS.md and A2A in the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation
A fact that names a version or a list is fast
Route: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, other clouds, open weights, coding agents, objections, numbers
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: C, a private eval on the team's own repos and tickets
A trusts the vendor's frame; B misses the question; D dismisses evidence
Tell: a decision about their work needs a test on their work
Five to remember: Six layers: compare like with like
Benchmark: who ran it, what it measures, contaminated or saturated
Nobody leads everywhere: name the board and the source type
Menlo: investor, survey, API spend only
Quote slow facts; check prices, ranks, versions, cloud line-ups
Recap: conversation tells: "Their model is better" → better at which layer, for which job?
Launch post → whose harness, which version, what cost per task?
Leaderboard → preference or task success? crowded near the ceiling?
Menlo, either way → investor link and API-only scope
"Our cloud decides" → what's on the commitment?
Version number in a fact → check before repeating
